PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349


APPLICATION OF ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND LCRA TRANSMISSION SERVICES CORPORATION TO AMEND THEIR CERTIFICATES OF CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY FOR THE BELL COUNTY EAST SWITCH TO BIG HILL SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE PROJECT IN BELL, BURNET, CONCHO, CORYELL, LAMPASAS, LLANO, MASON, MCCULLOCH, MENARD, MILAM, MILLS, SAN SABA, SCHLEICHER, TOM GREEN, AND WILLIAMSON COUNTIES§

BEFORE THE

STATE OFF OF ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS


INTERVENOR SUSAN BURROW’S
POST-HEARING BRIEF
I, Susan Burrow, a pro-se intervenor and Party No. 456, timely file this post-hearing brief to The State Office of Administrative Hearings (“SOAH”) Docket No. 473-26-16349, Public Utilities Commission of Texas (PUCT) Docket, No. 59475, and ONCOR (Egnyte system).
INTRODUCTION
I humbly request that the SOAH Judges and the PUC Commissioner consider the fact that I am a pro-se intervenor, and have no experience in dealing with legal court matters, and especially with writing official court documents required for hearings, court decisions, etc.  I humbly request that, should I include something that is not meant to be said in this case, or if something is not in correct format. that the Judges let my brief be submitted, heard, and kept in the record.  
ARGUMENTS
My husband and I, and approximately 1400 other families, are impacted by the lines that were added after the public meetings were held in June 2025, in September of 2025.  I contend that we were not properly notified in accordance with TAC 22.52, and we were not given the opportunity to voice our opinions and concerns in a public meeting.  
We received our notice on 5 April 2026.  By then, the Applicants had filed their request for the CNN for the project that had a total of 1200 variations of routes, that included over 400 miles of newly added routes, of which most include three links that impact our property directly, G71, G72 and G73.  These three segments of line appear in an overwhelmingly large number of variations of routes.  We had just three weeks to wrap our heads around what this massive project entailed.  In that short timeframe, with no legal experience, we struggled to figure out what we needed to do next.  We first tried to contact several law firms, only to find they were already hired by others with the same issue.  We had to learn how to become an intervenor, and respond to route adequacy challenge, and direct testimony of the Applicants.  We were thrown into a legal battle, with no legal knowledge or experience.  Our world came became totally turned upside-down when we opened that envelope containing the notice on 5 April 2026.   
The Applicant stated in the hearing it complied with the public meeting requirement as outlined in TAC 22.52.  However, the three public meetings were held nine months prior to submitting their application in June 2025.  In those meetings, the routes discussed did not include over 400 miles of new routes that were added in September 2025.  In my opinion, it would have been the right thing to do to hold another public meeting to address the concerns of the people living on the new routes.  The Applicants had plenty of time and resources to hold another more relevant, updated meeting, but they did not.  We, the people on those routes, around 1400 of us, were left in the dark.  We were blindsided.  We did not get to attend a public meeting.  We did not have almost a year - like the other folks did, to find legal help, and prepare to fight for our rights, and our homes. We should not have to be burdened with this project at all.
In addition to no public meetings for people of the 400 miles of new routes, the Applicants did not comply with TAC 22.52 by failing to notify all impacted landowners on these routes.  The Applicant did not use current Tax roll data and therefore, some landowners did not get a notice until well after the deadline when the Applicants were told that they missed these residents.  The Applicants failed to apply prudent avoidance, as well as disregarded community value when they proposed a route beside an elementary school having over 500 children and staff, and a church.     
Link G71 splits our property in half and consumes the areas, where for years, we dreamed of having our grown children build their homes for their families.  Link G72 runs directly along our property line, destroying the beautiful view over the valley that caused us to buy this property 35 years ago.  Link G73 turns from the corner of our property towards three of our neighbor's homes, the Gulbranson's, and the Van Der Boom's, and the Hoffman's (also Intervenors).  The Gulbranson home, is a homeschool for their four children.  The lines would be not more than 250 feet from the porch of their new home.  With the construction of the lines, these neighbors will be faced with tremendous hardship in having to relocate after just building their homes. Based on the large number of route variations that include these links, it if clear the Applicant did not consider the impacts of geographic diversity in this case. And they did not, in my opinion, consider community values.
The Applicant filed a Motion objecting to the testimonies of over 800 intervenors based on their testimonies containing their concerns about the impacts to the value of their land after condemnation, health effects of the EMF exposure, adverse effects to their farming and ranching, and wildlife management endeavors (Item 4726, PUC Interchange).  Their justification is that the testimonies may reference an article in a newspaper, magazine, website, etc. where the author is not a witness in this case, and therefore, the testimony is labeled "hearsay".  I ask, is it reasonable that the pro-se landowner be expected to present such Doctors and experts to the court for each such concern?  Moreover, regarding impacts to farming, ranching, and wildlife management, even the Applicants realize the knowledge and experience and expertise that farmers and ranchers have when it comes to their land, especially those that have managed land that's been in their families for decades.  What better expert than the person that has done the job for many years.  
The applicant also I ask that these discounted people be considered in your decision regarding this project.  
In the hearing, there was discussion regarding the need of Import Path 2 by 2038 vs. 2030.  There was discussion about the need altogether, and that the Applicant had not justified and proven the need.  I would like to reference ERCOT's Permian Basin Reliability Plan Study.  I am not an expert in electrical loads by any means, however, looking at the chart i that is the breakdown of the total 11,695 MW of "Additional Non-Oil and Gas Loads", 59% of the load is Cryto-currency, and 6% is Data Center.  It is no secret that President Trump issued a mandate in March 2026 to data centers to basically generate their own power.  Regulators are allowing data centers to connect directly to power plants or use their own on-site generation.  Again, I'm no expert, but I tend to think this would likely result in a decreased amount of energy needing to be transported across the state.  It is my opinion it would be prudent for the PUCT to step back from this extremely rushed process, take a pause, and re-evaluate the need for all of the proposed Import Paths, especially Import Path 2, since it was questioned in the hearing whether it was needed as early as 2030 (the original timeline was 2038).  Would it not be better to do this before the citizens are burdened with increase to their electric bills to help pay for the project, and before hundreds of thousands of our beautiful Texas landscape, and our homes are sacrificed forever? 
CONCLUSION
I pray that the SOAH and the PUCT will defend me, my family, and my fellow landowners, and our property rights.  I ask that you listen to our concerns.  Our concerns about our health, the depreciation of our land's value, our wildlife, our cattle, etc., is not "hearsay".  They are very REAL concerns.   
My family and I are faced with very serious hardships if links G71, G72, or G73 happen.  We will be forced with having to relocate, due to the EMF exposure, and decimation of our land use with the placement of the lines.  I do not believe all the medical journals and studies out there are "hearsay". Personally, my medical issues warrant my reluctance to live beside the lines.  Our children, who had plans to build here, are not wanting to raise their young children beside the lines. Our hopes and dreams of having our children and their families on the land beside us will be crushed.   G71, if built, will slice our property right down the middle, devaluing our property on both sides, will be with a few hundred feet of our home, and will significantly hamper our wildlife management efforts.  
I humbly ask that the Administration Law Judges deny the application, or at the very least pause Import Path 2 so that alternative solutions can be researched and discovered.  I also ask that if all efforts and arguments presented by all parties fail to convince the judges to deny the application, that they consider the hardships of my family and neighbors and not allow G71, G72, and G73 to be constructed. 





Respectfully submitted,
Susan Burrow
By:   /s/   Susan Burrow	
(Date Signed: June 19, 2026)
16265 Cedar Valley Road
Salado, Texas 76571
Telephone: (254) 702-2422
Email: sburrow91@gmail.com
